subject.title: improve(ui): restructure Settings around user-facing pages with full agent parity

question: Should OpenClaw make `ui.prefs` a synced persisted configuration contract and permit the system agent, behind exact-operation approval, to mutate nearly all non-denylisted configuration including tools and safe plugin entries?
rationale: This changes the long-term configuration, cross-device synchronization, and privileged-operation boundary; tests can validate mechanics but cannot choose the intended product and security policy.

options.title: Approve the bounded parity policy
options.body: Keep `ui.prefs` and the narrowed denylist, after repairing the regressions and documenting upgrade and approval behavior.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Land the settings IA separately and retain browser-local preferences or a smaller agent-write allowlist until the broader policy has dedicated design review.

options.title: Pause the policy expansion
options.body: Split or defer the persisted preference and system-agent authorization changes if maintainers do not want this new configuration boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded parity policy
recommendation.body: Keep `ui.prefs` and the narrowed denylist, after repairing the regressions and documenting upgrade and approval behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and authored the integrated settings and system-agent policy changes, so they are the best available owner to route the intended scope decision.
